hook.h2: The first words He ever spoke were light
hook.text: Then our Father said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
hook.note: Open any other Bible at Genesis 1 and those four words look exactly like the sentence around them — the same black ink as the genealogies. Here they are blue, because our Father said them. That is the whole idea, and you can see it working from the third verse of the book. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking, and until now you had no way of knowing which.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.

The Father's Heart Bible is a fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek — not an adaptation of any existing English Bible — made so you can hear God as He truly is: not a distant deity, but your Father.

And it is the first Bible in print to show you which words a divine person spoke, and which person spoke them. Our Father's words are in blue. The Son's are in red. The Spirit's are in purple. Not a red-letter New Testament with a black Old Testament, and not a study section at the back — full color on every page, Genesis to Revelation.

For a hundred and twenty-five years red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and until now those words were printed in the same ink as everything else. You could read the Bible your whole life and never notice how much of it is your Father talking to you.
This is the General Audience edition: the complete Bible, with no audience named on the cover. Some people want a Bible made for who they are. Some just want the Bible. This is that one.
It comes in three cover colors — Charcoal, Plum and White — in paperback or hardback, and in a Large Print edition set for easier reading.

Inside you will find a presentation page for a name, opening pages on intimacy, identity, inheritance and hearing His voice, an introduction to every one of the 66 books, and a Father's note closing each one with a short prayer. There are 1,354 study notes across 777 chapters: 1,075 explaining a word, name, custom or background, 248 marking where the text reveals the Father, and 31 recording a difference among the manuscripts.
Nothing is abridged. All 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses, governed by 170 written translation rules.
The text itself is free. Every word can be read online at no cost, by anyone, anywhere, in twenty-five languages. Print exists for the people who want to hold it, mark it, and hand it to someone.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

long.h: Receive The Father. Hear His Voice. His Heart Is For You.
body: Most of us learned about God before we ever met a Father. We learned rules, and roles, and a name that describes what He is rather than who He is. "God" is not a name. It is a category. Father is who He is — the name Jesus came to reveal.

The Father's Heart Bible was translated to let that come through. Not by softening the text, and not by adding to it, but by rendering the original languages so the relationship in them is not lost in translation.
This is the first Bible in print to color the divine voice by person. Our Father's words in blue. The Son's in red. The Spirit's in purple. Every book, every chapter, from the first page to the last.

The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation. His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored. Once you have seen a page this way it is difficult to go back to one where every voice looks the same.

Every book opens with an introduction and closes with a Father's note and a short prayer — so you are never dropped into Leviticus or Habakkuk without knowing why it is there.

faq.q: How is this different from the targeted editions?
faq.a: It is the same complete Bible and the same translation. The targeted editions — the Dad's Bible, the Teen Bible, the Soldier's Bible and the rest — carry a cover and opening pages written for one reader. This one names no audience. If you want a Bible that speaks to who someone is, choose a targeted edition. If you just want the Bible, this is it.

faq.q: Which cover color should I choose?
faq.a: They are identical inside. Charcoal is the quiet one and the most common choice for a personal copy; Plum reads warmer and is the one most often bought as a gift; White is the brightest on a shelf and photographs best for a presentation. Every color is available in paperback and hardback.

Paperback if you are going to carry it, mark it and not feel precious about it. Hardback if it is going into someone's hands as a gift, or onto a shelf for years. The interior is the same 876 pages in full color either way.

faq.q: Should I get regular or large print?
faq.a: Both are 6 x 9 and both carry the complete Bible in Divine Voice Color with all 1,354 study notes. The Large Print edition sets the type larger for easier reading, which makes the book thicker. If you read for long stretches, or you are buying for a parent or grandparent, choose Large Print.

faq.q: Is the color really on every page?
faq.a: Yes — Genesis to Revelation, in full color throughout. Not a red-letter New Testament with a black Old Testament, and not a color section at the back. You can see it for yourself, free, at fathersheartbible.com/read.
